articles.title: Ohio State Holds Senior Day Before Opener, Ryan Day Explains Changing Season-Ending Tradition
articles.summary: Ohio State flipped the script when it came to Senior Day for the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
Ohio State flipped the script when it came to Senior Day for the 2026 college football season.

The Buckeyes honored their senior class in Saturday's opener against Ball State, which is the exact opposite for how the tradition is typically handled.

Coach Ryan Day told reporters in August that OSU administrators came to him with the idea. They concluded it was one less thing to worry about while preparing for the final home game against Michigan on Nov. 28.

"When we look at all the things that go on that weekend, the way things have changed, there are some things that we thought about," he said. "The first thing was, we want to keep much of the focus on The Game, and the more distractions we have — there's already enough distractions during that week — so this was just one more thing that we felt like we could move."

Day added the Ohio State seniors were in alignment with the plan.

Former Buckeyes players and others expressed a different feeling toward the change. Traditions that span multiple generations are what helps to set college sports apart, and senior day is one such rite of passage.

Granted, the ongoing evolution of college athletics has removed some of the pageantry from senior day.

It's becoming increasingly rare that players spend four or five years at one school, especially at a program as big as Ohio State. One could argue Day's decision further cheapens the occasion.

Running back Ja'Kobi Jackson and safeties Earl Little Jr. and Terry Moore only transferred to OSU this offseason. They had yet to play a snap for the Buckeyes before the school staged its senior day.

Should the Buckeyes go on to beat Michigan, that may increase the likelihood a Week 1 senior day becomes the norm in Columbus. Day could reverse course if Ohio State, sans what's supposedly a distraction, comes up short against its biggest rival during Thanksgiving weekend.

articles.title: Man City 1-0 Coventry: Erling Haaland ensures perfect Premier League record is preserved under Enzo Maresca
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Erling Haaland scored a first-half winner to ensure Man City stay perfect in the Premier League; battling Coventry remain winless after three played, having failed to score in any of those games
articles.body:
The Norwegian has found the net 20 times in as many outings against Premier League newcomers, only failing against Sunderland last term. His towering header on this occasion was enough for all three points.

Man City might have spent a league-high £440m on new signings during the window, two making their debuts against Coventry, but it's undoubtedly Haaland who remains their greatest difference-maker.

£125m-rated Enzo Fernandez, a deadline day arrival, was involved in the goal. He was a late stand-in for Nico O'Reilly after the 21-year-old was injured in the warm-up, and showed his worth with a classy introductory performance. His pass to release Antoine Semenyo was the precursor to Haaland's decisive strike, scored in the 26th minute.

Coventry spent the remainder of the contest making life difficult for the home side. Summer addition Taiwo Awoniyi fluffed his chance of a one-on-one with Gianluigi Donnarumma, steering wide, while the City goalkeeper also made huge saves to rebuff Jack Rudoni's header at the back post and Ellis Simms late on.

Frank Lampard's side are yet to score a goal since their long-awaited return to the top flight. They came very close at the Etihad. But City's ruthless finisher had the final say with his 300th club goal. He continues to be undeniable as Man City move temporarily top of the Premier League - displacing Arsenal before they play Chelsea on Super Sunday .

"I was pleased with the win, for different reasons. We kept them [Coventry] alive. We couldn't score one or two more, at least. We suffer together until the end; not all the wins are going to be nice. We need these kinds of wins.

"It was a little bit of an ugly win. It's something we need and a clean sheet is important."

On the performance of Enzo Fernandez : "Enzo only arrived two days ago; he's been frustrated the last two or three weeks.

"In the end he plays from the start and I'm quite happy. We've shared time together, so it's easier because we know each other very well. And I know he's going to help us win games."

Lampard vows not to lose belief despite tough start

"Good performance from us. Felt like we deserved something from the game. Our defensive organisation was great. We created moments of pressure, three big chances. The players took on the challenge really well; they are disappointed and so am I.

"I never criticise players, because I understand pressure. This is the level. It's the brutal reality of it. But we don't play Manchester City every week. The Premier League is a high level, but on reflection there is a lot of good to use in our mentality.

"Against Arsenal it felt like a first Premier League game in 25 years. Today felt like a competitive Premier League team coming with a clear idea and threat. The fixture list has been tough on us. We can't lose belief off the back of three games and so we must look forward."

articles.title: Brighton 1-1 Leeds: Luka Vuskovic cancels out Jayden Bogle's opener as Daniel Farke's side rue missed chances
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Brighton held Leeds 1-1 after the visitors missed so many chances; Jayden Bogle put Leeds ahead for the Whites' first goal at Brighton in 12 years; Dominic Calvert-Lewin missed  big chances along with Anton Stach and Ao Tanaka, as Luka Vuskovic levelled
articles.body:
Leeds have had no joy at Brighton in recent years - their last win at the south coast club came in 2009 and they went eight games without a goal at the home of the Seagulls, dating back to 2012.

But Jayden Bogle ended that run by tapping home from close range after Ao Tanaka kept the ball alive following Bart Verbruggen's save to deny Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Leeds striker Calvert-Lewin should have had a first-half hat-trick, putting a one-on-one wide early on before seeing an effort cleared off the line by Lewis Dunk after rounding Verbruggen in the minutes following Bogle's opener.

Tanaka then hit the bar almost immediately after that chance, before the Leeds midfielder had an effort ruled out for offside after the break. Anton Stach also had a close-range effort well saved as the chances grew.

But as Leeds missed chances, Brighton's confidence grew. After Malick Yalcouye and Charalampos Kostoulas went close, Luka Vuskovic got off the mark at his new club by heading home from a corner.

Brighton could have won it when Promise David was found in the box but he fired over - then Pascal Gross missed an even bigger chance as he scooped over from four yards out.

But the most wasteful team on the day were Leeds, who ended up with an Expected Goals tally of 2.66 - but ended up with only one goal and one point.

The key moments from the Amex Stadium...

5: BIG CHANCE! Calvert-Lewin breaks through on goal but sidefoots the one-on-one wide. The offside flag goes up on the Leeds striker, but replays show it may have counted.

15: GOAL! Calvert-Lewin has a close-range header saved by Bart Verbruggen but Ao Tanaka pulls it back across for Bogle to tap home on the goal line.

23: OFF THE LINE! Calvert-Lewin thinks he has made it 2-0 when he rounds Verbruggen but Dunk clears his shot from off the goal line.

24: OFF THE BAR! From the resulting corner, Tanaka strikes the bar after being found unmarked at the back post.

27: CLOSE! Pascal Gross nearly levels for Brighton when his sliced free-kick flies just over James Trafford's bar.

29: SAVE! Brighton get their first shot on target when Olivier Boscagli's crossfield pass is volleyed at goal by Diego Gomez, but Trafford saves at the near post.

49: BIG CHANCE! A long throw falls into Anton Stach's path but his close-range effort is saved by Verbruggen.

51: GOAL DISALLOWED! Tanaka thinks he has a second as he turns home Stach's free-kick but he is caught offside by the linesman and VAR.

54: JUST WIDE! Gross curls an effort just wide of goal as Brighton's confidence grows after that disallowed goal.

68: SAVE! Kostoulas goes on a mazy run into the Leeds penalty area but fires straight at Trafford in the crucial moment.

69: SAVE! Yalcouye sees an effort saved as Brighton's pressure continues to grow.

71: GOAL! The pressure finally tells as Vuskovic heads in De Cuyper's corner from a few yards out.

85: BIG MISS! Promise David comes off the bench and nearly wins it but he heads over Boscagli's cross.

89: A BIGGER MISS! Gross scoops over from four yards out in the last big chance of the game.

Farke: It's a good point but we should put this game to bed

Leeds head coach Daniel Farke to Sky Sports:

"Brighton away is always a good point, especially if you look at our recent history as a club in the last one or two decades. It's definitely a good point. Brighton are a good team and are in some very good form.

"It was also a missed chance not to win it today. At half-time we should have been out of sight. In such a difficult away game, you miss so many clear-cut chances. I'm sure in the Expected Goals we were way higher than them - although in the second half they were also pushing for the equaliser.

"There was also an unlucky goal scored by Ao Tanaka which was one inch offside. Normally in such a game, you will lose it. So happy we go home with something in our hands.

"Dominic should have put the game to bed in the first half, Anton in the second, Lukas as well and the offside goal - so we had many, many good situations. But Brighton is a good side. So if you don't put the game to bed, they have the chance with dominating possession to come back into the game. But it was overall a good performance from my team.

"Five points after these three difficult starting games is quite impressive. Also success in the cup game vs Nottingham - so we want to ride this momentum as much as possible. No one can take away these five points. They're crucial - and also the confidence from these five points."

Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler to Sky Sports:

"First half we had a lack of intensity and energy. Second half we showed a different phase and intensity. We won the personal duels and the second balls.

"It's also about first, outrunning the opponent, doing the basics of the football game, and then being a good football team in possession. Today, we started with a different mindset - the wrong mindset. And then we changed it. And you could see how fast we could change the game.

"What my team stands for is real character; they always stick together. They face adversity and they did it again today. So I'm very impressed with the reaction from my team. We will find answers, find solutions - and then become a physical team from the beginning."

Analysis: Brighton defenders put in superhuman effort

Pascal Struijk may have been disappointed not to feature more than his two-minute cameo against former club Leeds. But in fairness, there is absolutely no spot in the Brighton defence for him to get into.

Despite being signed to replace the outgoing Jan Paul Van Hecke, Struijk had to sit and watch the centre-back pairing of Luka Vuskovic and Lewis Dunk put in a mammoth shift against his former team.

Vuskovic scored the crucial leveller for Brighton - showing the attacking prowess he demonstrated in the Bundesliga at Hamburg last season. But Dunk was arguably player of the match, and helped keep the scoreline down.

The Brighton captain was everywhere throughout - making 12 clearances, twice as many as the next-best Seagulls player. The best of the dozen came to deny Dominic Calvert-Lewin from off the line in a goal-saving challenge.

And there's no spot for Struijk at left-back, given Olivier Boscagli's display in that role. Brighton's best chances came from his wand of a left boot - as he created five chances against Leeds - which was just as many as the entire Whites starters combined.

articles.title: Bristol Rovers 1-0 Rotherham
articles.summary: Steve Evans came out on top as his Bristol Rovers side won 1-0 against his former club Rotherham in Sky Bet League Two.
articles.body:
The outstanding Tommy Leigh made the difference in the 32nd minute as Rovers scored via the first shots on target in the game.

Leigh deftly flicked the ball over the top of the Millers defence to play in Pirates winger Bobby Kamwa down the left. He cut into the box only to shoot tamely at Ted Cann's near post, but the ball rebounded off the goalkeeper nicely for Leigh to slot home just inside the box.

Rotherham midfielder Brandon Cover shot straight at keeper Brad Young in the 39th minute and Shaq Forde threatened from outside the area shortly before the break, set up again after more good work from Leigh, his last action before being substituted at the break for Ellis Harrison.

Cann then pushed Kofi Balmer's close-range shot onto the crossbar before Fabio Tavares headed substitute Aaron Nemane's cross straight at Young nine minutes later, going even closer by hitting the bar from close range in the final seconds.

Rovers held on for a third home win in the league this season, as Alex Bruce and Rovers assistant manager Paul Raynor were sent off following an off-pitch melee in stoppage time.

articles.title: Fulham 2-3 Crystal Palace: Pierre Sage off the mark as Eagles come from behind at winless Cottagers
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Crystal Palace win 3-2 at Fulham; Pierre Sage records his first victory as Eagles head manager, while Alvaro Arbeola remains winless as Fulham boss
articles.body:
The pressure was on Sage and his Fulham counterpart Alvaro Arbeloa heading into this London derby at Craven Cottage after defeats in each of their first two Premier League games.

However, it was the Frenchman who was all smiles at the full-time whistle as he punched the air in front of jubilant Palace fans in the away end after this unlikely three points.

In stark contrast, however, Arbeola will be left scratching his head at just how his side lost this game having led at the break and finishing with an impressive xG of 3.13, with youngster Josh King outstanding once again.

But the defeat means the Cottagers have now lost their opening three matches of a top-flight campaign for just the third time, worryingly being relegated on both previous occasions in 1951/52 and 2020/21.

11: GOAL! King makes the early breakthrough after Oscar Bobb's run to the byline and Jaydee Canvot's crucial deflection that left Dean Henderson helpless.

14: GOAL RULED OUT ! Daichi Kamada thinks he has immediately levelled matters after touching home Yeremy Pino's cross from the left, only for a tight VAR call to go against the Japan midfielder.

33: SAVE! Henderson shows impressive near-post reactions to keep out Timothy Castagne's close-range effort in front of England boss Thomas Tuchel.

35: GOAL! Eddie Nketiah feeds Mitchell in space down the left and the full back blasts a powerful drive past Leno at his near post.

42: GOAL! Palacios restores the hosts' lead just before half-time after great work down the left from King to dummy Richards, with the midfielder in the right place to smash home after Henderson had denied Gonzalo Garcia.

54: GOAL! Mitchell nets his second of the game, although only after Garcia somehow failed to clear his weak effort.

77: GOAL! Chilwell completes the comeback after Leno appeared to bring down Khalaili, only for the sub to stroke home into the empty net.

"Three games, three losses, so it's difficult, and now you are thinking that we have to go to Anfield, Manchester United is coming to Craven Cottage, so you can see two very difficult games.

"Also in the Carabao Cup we have to go face West Ham United, so not easy, but we knew this month it was going to be a very tough month.

"But I told my players this month will not define our entire season. I think they are working so hard, they are giving everything they have, and with this mentality, with this character, I am sure that win will come."

"I have to accept the story of today because that was the context of the game," he said when asked about the openness of the match.

"But I have to change things and to improve the way of defending with the players, because we were too open in the first half and not very well-coordinated.

"That's why they scored the second goal especially, but they had a lot of opportunities, and we took the first goal after a mistake in the build-up and we have to improve that too.

"That's why today the lesson is free, because we won, but we are aware of the conditions of this victory."

articles.title: Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland suffers 'significant' hamstring injury
articles.summary: Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland is set for a spell on the sidelines after picking up a "significant" hamstring injury in Saturday's Scottish Premiership victory over Motherwell.
articles.body:
Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland is set for a spell on the sidelines after picking up a "significant" hamstring injury in Saturday's Scottish Premiership victory over Motherwell.

The Scotland striker limped off after eight minutes at Ibrox, with his replacement Ryan Naderi scoring the only goal of the game shortly after.

Shankland - who signed from Hearts in May - has scored four goals in his first 10 Rangers appearances, but will now miss several weeks in a blow to Derek McInnes.

"It looks quite significant, to be honest," manager McInnes said.

"It's a similar injury we think that he had at Hearts last January. That was a period of time that he was out with that.

"We'll get the scan done on Monday and see how it looks then rather than speculating. It's disappointing because he was leading the line and scoring a few goals in the last couple of games.

"There were more positives than negatives from today, but that was a negative."

articles.title: Terzic: "Me ha gustado todo del equipo y la atmósfera de San Mamés ha sido increíble"
articles.standfirst: El técnico disfruta y se suelta para descubrir cuál es el amuleto que lleva en los partidos
articles.summary: El técnico disfruta y se suelta para descubrir cuál es el amuleto que lleva en los partidos
articles.body: El Athletic devolvió la sonrisa a sus aficionados con una victoria de prestigio ante el Atlético. "Estoy muy contento y satisfecho. Has ido un partido muy intenso con grandes momentos y es un gran resultado. Me ha gustado todo de mi equipo y la atmósfera en San Mamés ha sido increíble. Ha sido increíble como lo hemos afrontado y después de la pausa de hidratación y del descanso el equipo ha estado increíble", resaltó Terzic. El alemán premió a la plantilla con una jornada más de descanso.Volverán a entrenar el martes. Las sensaciones del triunfo: “Siempre es bueno ganar partido y también hacerlo en casa. Doy las gracias a San Mamés por el ambiente. Esta noche vamos a dormir muy satisfechos, pero estos seis puntos no son más que el inicio de la temporada. Toca ya preparar el siguiente partido”. Nico y Sancet: “Podemos hablar de Nico, pero también de Oihan, que ha jugado en cuatro posiciones diferentes. Él puede ser uno de los mejores jugadores de la Liga. Y también puedo hablar de una buena parada de Unai. Estoy muy contento con toda la plantilla y también con el trabajo de todo el staff técnico”. Un equipo de varios registros: “No es mi Athletic, es nuestro Athletic y lo que la gente quiere ver. Queremos un equipo preparado para luchar y ganar los partidos. Las diferentes estructuras es algo necesario en el mundo del fútbol”. Los cambios de esquema: “No es difícil si tienes buenos jugadores. Los cinco cambios por partido te hacen estar preparado para adaptarte al partido. Esta vez hemos conseguido mantener también la portería a cero por segundo partido consecutivo”. La lucha por los puestos altos: “El equipo está preparado para luchar. No puedo prometer dónde llegaremos, pero el equipo sí ha merecido lo que tiene”. El amuleto de Terzic: “Siempre lo llevo en el bolsillo. Es un imán, de mi hija. Tengo dos hijas muy hermosas y siempre lo tengo conmigo. No es la razón por la que ganamos, pero siempre la tengo conmigo”.

articles.title: El Athletic repite hoja de ruta y sentencia en un puñado de segundos
articles.standfirst: Los leones encadenan dos triunfos sin recibir goles y marcan tras buenos ajustes técnicos
articles.summary: Los leones encadenan dos triunfos sin recibir goles y marcan tras buenos ajustes técnicos
articles.body: La segunda victoria del Athletic en esta Liga llegó en un minuto de felicidad. Igual que ocurrió en Vigo, donde 104 segundos fueron determinantes para que los leones tomasen una ventaja definitiva ante el Celta, el Athletic se merendó al Atlético en poco más de un minuto. Primero fue Nico Williams y después Robert Navarro, los dos tras asistencia de Iñaki Williams, los que martillearon la portería de Oblak. ¡Qué celebración en San Mamés! El griterío fue espectacular en una grada que en su tribuna sur alta tuvo al homenajeado equipo Genuine. Lier Basabe Barturen, uno de sus capitanes, fue de los que festejó como si le fuera la vida en ello. El Athletic encadena dos triunfos consecutivos y concluye la cuarta jornada con la mitad de los puntos amasados de todos los que se habían puesto en juego. Este 6 de 12 con victorias ante el Atlético y el Celta y derrotas frente a Sevilla y Barcelona deja en muy buen lugar al equipo de Terzic, que en una semana afrontará tres citas claves antes del extenso parón de selecciones. Los leones jugarán los dos siguientes sábados en San Mamés ante Elche y Alavés para entre medio medirse de visitantes al Levante. En un partido en el que hubo alrededor de 5.000 asientos libres -¿tendría algo que ver en ello la masiva retirada de invitaciones que ha realizado Uriarte?- los de Terzic se mostraron como un equipo en crecimiento. No tanto como para encargar mármol de Carrara para levantar una estatua en previsión de sus futuros éxitos, que lo de disfrutar con las buenas sensaciones cotiza al alza, pero sí para conformar que el equipo ha tomado la senda del mejor de los caminos. Terzic apretó a sus futbolistas en el descanso para que tuvieran una entrada generosa en la segunda mitad. Y los futbolistas siguieron el mensaje. Nico regresó al gol en la Liga, que no marcaba desde el triunfo del pasado torneo ante el Alavés, y Robert Navarro continuó con el camino que había abierto días atrás en Vigo. El 2-0 cogió a Terzic tomando apuntes para hacer correcciones en la disposición del equipo a partir de la primera ventaja. Vio el tanto de refilón y lo celebró con rabia. Los cambios que siguieron después fue para ordenar el esquema y las variantes trabajadas durante la semana. También a partir de los cambios que hizo Simeone. Y el 3-0 hizo justicia a su predicción de víspera de que Sancet marcaría pronto.

articles.title: Millwall 4-0 Bolton Wanderers: Lyndon Dykes scores twice for Lions as both sides finish with 10 men
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Millwall and Bolton Wanderers at The Den on Saturday; Lyndon Dykes scores twice in Lions win as both sides finish with 10 men.
articles.body:
The Lions made light of the fact they have 11 first team players currently unavailable - and that their last two games ended in heavy defeat - as they inflicted a third loss in a row on the Trotters.

A late burst of three goals in nine minutes gave the final score an emphatic look, while both teams finished with 10 men after Millwall midfielder Jenson Metcalfe and Bolton captain Josh Sheehan were sent off for violent conduct.

Bolton had a big chance to grab an early lead when Sam Dalby played a one-two with Sheehan before scuffing wide from inside the box.

The away side were growing in confidence as Sheehan had time to control before getting away a shot that was held by Millwall goalkeeper Max Crocombe.

But it was Millwall who claimed a much-needed lead in the 38th minute when Metcalfe hung up a corner to the back post where Caleb Taylor rose highest to head in.

Dykes almost doubled the advantage early in the second half with an audacious lob from 40 yards that Bolton goalkeeper Jack Bonham was relieved to see drop over his crossbar.

The Trotters then came close to an equaliser twice in the space of a minute, with Crocombe first having to make a good save to turn an effort from half-time substitute Ruben Rodrigues behind.

The resulting corner was then cleared as far as Xavier Simons who crashed a tremendous first-time strike from just outside the box against the bar.

Millwall then had a big chance to make the game safe when debutant Yanis Issoufou's backheel put Jordi Osei-Tutu through, but Bonham stood tall to make an important save.

Taylor then fluffed an opportunity to score his second after Metcalfe's free-kick was allowed to run through to him before Gale's shot across goal needed tipping behind by Crocombe at the other end.

The Lions then made the game safe in the 83rd minute when Bonham allowed Dykes to nick a harmless-looking Camiel Neghli long ball off his toes and walk the ball into the net.

There were then a pair of red cards three minutes later when Metcalfe and Sheehan were both sent off after getting into a fight.

Dykes added his second in the 88th minute when he beat Bonham at his near post after Zak Sturge had nipped in ahead of Max Conway in the Bolton area.

And there was still time for the Lions to score a fourth in stoppage time when Issoufou played the ball through for Neghli to apply a composed finish.

"As far as I'm concerned, the kid dragged his boot over the top of Jenson's head.

"I think Jenson thought he tried to kick him in the head - whether he did or not, the lad (Sheehan) can only answer that himself.

"After that, it was handbags, everybody starts coming in and it's just a kerfuffle.

"A week's a long time in football, isn't it? A week ago, we'd just come off the back of Bristol [City] and Norwich and we're all thinking 'here we go.'

"Then we lose a couple of games, we sell Femi [Azeez, to Brighton] at the end of the window, then we lose 10 or 12 players [to injury].

"So, it's been a testing week, and there's been a bit of frustration in that we can't put our best foot forward, in terms of competing and trying to win games.

"But I thought today was really important for us to have a good reaction."

"I think it's an unnecessary red card, on our point, because when Josh falls on top of Metcalfe and drags him on top of him, I was right in front of it.

"He hasn't made any movement to move his leg towards the player's head, it was just a natural sort of momentum, the way he falls on top of him.

"Then I think because of Metcalfe's reaction, and the way the melee happened, with so many players involved in it, the referee thinks it's more of an issue than it actually was.

"If they just zoom in and have a look at it, they'll see it, so hopefully that'll get rescinded.

"We lost a man to injury after we made all our subs, so that gave them a numerical advantage when we were chasing the game.

"Up until the 83rd minute, when Lewis Brunt went off [injured], we were more than a match for Millwall."

articles.title: Sheffield United 1-3 Norwich City: Mohamed Toure on target in Canaries win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Sheffield United and Norwich City at Bramall Lane on Saturday; Anthony Musaba, Mohamed Toure and Mathias Kvistgaarden all score in a comfortable win for the Canaries.
articles.body:
Goals from Anthony Musaba, Mohamed Toure and Mathias Kvistgaarden earned them the three points, with Patrick Bamford scoring for the hosts.

Musaba struck in the eighth minute with a curling effort. Goalkeeper Michael Cooper got a hand to the ball but could not keep it out.

The visitors maintained their early pressure with Andre Brooks screwing a shot wide and then putting another straight at Cooper. Playing against the team he left this summer, the lively Brooks also fired wide from a corner.

The Blades began to pose more of an attacking threat, with Sydie Peck forcing a save from Vladan Kovacevic at his near post and the keeper turning a Romelle Donovan shot wide.

The equaliser came in the 23rd minute when Ben Brereton Diaz found Tyrese Campbell and he laid the ball off to Bamford who beat Kovacevic with a curling effort from just outside the area.

Brereton Diaz shot wide and Campbell had a low shot saved before Norwich regained the lead a minute before the break. Anis Slimane sent Toure clear and the striker slipped the ball past Cooper one-on-one.

Cooper had to stand up well to Musaba, making an important save at his near post, while Toure failed to direct a header on target when the ball was whipped in from the left.

The fourth goal of the game came in the 62nd minute, with substitute Kvistgaarden finding the net with a low shot shortly after joining the action.

Hamza Choudhury appeared to have made a second goal-line clearance in rapid succession, but the referee ruled that the ball had crossed the line.

Sheffield United never looked likely to stage a comeback, with their attack lacklustre. Their best effort of the second half was a firm drive from substitute Kalvin Phillips which flew wide.

Ben Chrisene made a vital challenge to nick the ball away from Bamford in the area in the closing stages as Norwich defended resolutely.

The defeat was Sheffield United's first of the season in any competition.

"We didn't deserve anything from the game. Disappointed with the last 20 minutes. It really irritated me. It's not like us. We felt sorry for ourselves.

"I thought we made it pretty comfortable for Norwich. They managed the game well, managed the game better than us. And the goals that we've conceded are really, really poor, even though the third one's offside, which you'll see when that gets replayed.

"But, you know, even taking that out, I think Philippe would have been disappointed if he had not won the game today. I don't think we deserve to, especially in that last 20-25 minutes, get anything out of it.

"We never looked like getting back into the game and putting pressure on them and asking them the question.

"We got ourselves back in, scored a good goal, and then I thought from there we wrestled the initiative off them and it was on us. We got the press right, we didn't allow them to get out.

"The front three especially, in my opinion, one of the best in the division in how they play, we never allowed them to get the ball up to them because we shut that down, we wrestled the initiative back.

"You're going into 43 minutes and the game is just turned on its head, we don't get those opportunities to score those goals. They've had the opportunity to score the goals.

"Regardless of the offside decision or not, they were better than us in the second half."

"A lot of respect towards Chris (Wilder). The way he prepares his teams every time, they're always full of passion, really direct and it's hard to handle. So it was important to keep as much as possible control of the ball, not to give it away too easily.

"Although Sheffield United wanted to press us we came out really well several times, so that was an important part of this game.

"Of course, scoring the goals also. We take the lead just before half-time and it's an important momentum that you take.

"I'm very pleased about how the team controlled the game in the second half and we had the best chances there by far to score more goals. So to do that in an away game, with this crowd, with this manager also and the way he prepares his team, it's a really positive thing.

"We need to continue doing what we've been doing, making it better, integrating the new players, getting players out of injury, creating connections with all the players.

"Praise to Andre (Brooks) today. He came back to the club that he loves. It's like his family here. So that's a difficult one as a young player for the first time and he played a really good game.

"That's sometimes difficult because your emotions are sometimes bigger. But he did that really well. He played good."

articles.title: Portsmouth 2-0 Cardiff City: Conor Shaughnessy and Marko Milovanovic score in Pompey win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Portsmouth and Cardiff City at Fratton Park on Saturday; Conor Shaughnessy and Marko Milovanovic score as Pompey claim home win.
articles.body:
The south-coast side paid a poignant pre-match tribute to former goalkeeper Alan Knight, who sadly passed away this week aged 65.

Knight played 801 games for Pompey and also served them as coach and ambassador, and both sets of players lined up around the centre circle for an impeccably-observed minute's silence.

The hosts handed debuts to transfer deadline-day signings Tyrese Shade and Jayden Meghoma.

Cardiff could have opened the scoring after only three minutes when Krystian Bielik headed wide from a Joel Bagan free-kick.

Adrian Segecic had Pompey's first clear chance when his long-range effort was tipped wide by Nathan Trott following an initial poor clearance from the Cardiff goalkeeper.

Portsmouth should have taken the lead after 23 minutes when Marezi headed wide from close range.

A minute later Terry Devlin also failed to keep his header on target from Segecic's low free-kick.

The home side broke the deadlock 14 minutes before half-time when Shaughnessy sent a looping header into the net from new boy Shade's long throw.

Marezi then shanked another presentable chance wide from a tight angle after John Mousinho's men had hit Cardiff on the counter-attack.

Serbian Marezi made amends for his first-half misses by doubling Pompey's lead seven minutes after the re-start.

Segecic picked out Marezi with a pin-point cross and the big striker swept the ball past the helpless Trott.

Marezi thought he had scored his second and Pompey's third when he nodded in Meghoma's cross, only for the goal to be ruled out for offside.

Pompey looked vulnerable defensively, but Cardiff lacked the killer edge to ever look like taking full advantage.

The second from bottom Bluebirds are still waiting for their first Championship win since last season's promotion from League One.

Frustrations boiled over in the final 15 minutes when Cardiff defender Bielik appeared to grab a home fan around the throat.

Pompey almost added a third when Abu Kamara was denied by the crossbar while captain Marlon Pack also had a header from a tight angle blocked.

Cian Ashford almost reduced the deficit in the last minute of the 90 but his shot from the edge of the penalty area proved no match for Pompey goalkeeper Daniel Bielica.

"I'm delighted with the result. It was completely different to the other performances, we didn't necessarily have a huge amount of control in the game, but I thought the first half was pretty good.

"The second half became a bit fractured, Cardiff changed their shape, which caused us a couple of problems.

"Thankfully for us, after we got the second goal, the game broke up a bit as there were quite a few stoppages which probably helped us just to kill the game off.

"You can't be perfect in everything that we do, we strive for that so there are going to be opportunities.

"We have been down in the dumps because of the results, the performances haven't been a million miles off it and there's loads we want to do better, I never ever want to hide behind that.

"We have to make sure we are level when we win games and level when we lose games - and just look for areas to improve because that's going to make us better."

"It was obviously a very disappointing result.

"We are not happy with the goals we conceded and there are a lot of areas where we can improve.

"We had enough chances to score but were not clinical enough.

"We were not aggressive enough defensively and we always knew it was going to be a very tough test.

"We are confident we can win games at this level, as long as we get the basics right."

articles.title: Portsmouth boss John Mousinho apologises to Cardiff City players over fan incident
articles.summary: Portsmouth head coach John Mousinho apologises to Cardiff City players after an incident involving home fans at Fratton Park during their Championship match.
articles.body:
Portsmouth head coach John Mousinho has apologised to Cardiff City players after an incident involving home fans at Fratton Park.

In the 72nd minute of Portsmouth's 2-0 Championship win over the Bluebirds, Cardiff defender Krystian Bielik got into a physical altercation with a fan as he went to retrieve a ball.

Cardiff head coach Brian Barry-Murphy claimed afterwards that Bielik "got slapped in the face", while clips circulating on social media appeared to show the Poland international grabbing a young fan around his upper body.

Several Portsmouth supporters made gestures that indicated they believed the fan had been grabbed around the throat.

In the aftermath, another fan threw a ball at the head of Cardiff defender Perry Ng, which resulted in both fans being ejected from the stadium.

Speaking after the match, Pompey boss Mousinho said: "The referee said that, as Krystian went to get the ball, there was a little bit of a kerfuffle and one of the supporters struck him.

"It wasn't a good incident. I have just seen him there, and he was OK, but that's not the point, we can't be having that.

"We want to create a really difficult atmosphere at Fratton Park, we have done that successfully over the past few years.

"Sometimes it tips over, I understand that, I don't think it needs to tip over to that extent.

"We extend our apologies to the players, Cardiff and make sure we can try to cut it out."

Portsmouth secure first home victory against winless Cardiff

Championship: Boro beat QPR to go second; West Ham ease past Derby; Burnley bottom after Bristol City defeat

Cardiff boss Barry-Murphy described the incident as "not acceptable", but applauded the officials for their handling of the situation.

"Krystian went to get the ball back from the stands and got slapped in the face," said Barry-Murphy.

"I just wanted to make sure he was protected and make sure he was OK. He is.

"I thought the referee and his staff handled the incident impeccably.

"I think the players are always subjected to different things, it's not acceptable what happens.

"They don't expect that sort of treatment. My job is to protect the players but really my focus is on trying to make sure that we play well and win.

"So I'm sure the club and the FA (Football Association) will look at this and implement the correct process."

articles.title: Indiana QB Josh Hoover finishes out touchdown drive vs. North Texas with bloody nose
articles.summary: A bad face mask penalty left Hoover with blood dripping down his face, but the quarterback persisted to grow the Hoosiers' lead.
articles.body:
Indiana's new first-string quarterback is putting his sweat and his blood on the field. In his first game since transferring from TCU , Josh Hoover powered through a bloody nose to score Indiana's third touchdown in a dominant showing against North Texas.

Hoover sustained the injury in the second quarter after being subjected to an egregious face mask foul, with his helmet getting pulled almost all the way around his head. In the process, the top of Hoover's nose got split, resulting in blood rushing down the quarterback's face.

Hoover, though, didn't stop playing on the drive, even as the blood dripped into his chinstrap and onto his white pants.

By staying in, though, Hoover was able to find Charlie Becker in the end zone to grow Indiana's lead.

Hoover then returned on the next drive with a bandage over his nose, seemingly cleaned up from the bloody outing. Indiana then scored a field goal on that drive to grow the lead to 24-6 before halftime.

Hoover, who was one of the highest-profile transfers this offseason, has been delivering early on as the defending champions get their season underway. The quarterback ended the first half with two touchdowns and just one incompletion, going 7-of-8 for 100 yards.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest 0-0 Tottenham: Expensive but misfiring Spurs still need to improve
articles.summary: Tottenham have failed to score in their opening three Premier League games and manager Roberto de Zerbi says it will take time to build his expensive squad into a team.
articles.body:
It has been more than half a century since Tottenham have gone this long without a league goal to start the season.

A City Ground stalemate at Nottingham Forest at least gets Roberto de Zerbi's side their first point of the season but not to the extent they would want.

It followed defeats to Brentford and Newcastle which means Spurs have failed to score in their opening three league games for the first time since 1974-75.

Spurs did not play badly - they were the better side - but after their huge summer transfer outlay more is needed and expected.

De Zerbi preached patience and he is right - 10 senior arrivals means his team is still to find an identity.

And they did leave Forest with a point, something they have failed to do for almost three years.

Indeed, the video assistant referee's call to rule out Neco Williams' bundled second-half effort ensured it was not a third-straight Premier League defeat for Spurs.

Yet they have now failed to score in three successive Premier League games for the first time since November 2021, and improvement is needed at misfiring Spurs.

Last March's 3-0 win for Forest at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium provided the platform for the visitors' survival bid while leaving Spurs floundering until the final day.

Since then Spurs have spent over £300m on new players - contributing to the record £3.49bn Premier League outlay this summer.

Sandro Tonali, Jon Paul Van Hecke, Savio and Omar Marmoush were the new signings who started on Saturday, with De Zerbi remaining calm after another blank.

"We bought very, very good players but you can't just build the team with the names like in Football Manager," he told Sky Sports.

"We are disappointed for the result but for the performance very happy. Considering we started to work together last Thursday for the first time, for the first day.

"We have to improve in every part of football, organisation with and without the ball. Even today I thought we defended very well.

"We have to work because I think we played very well with the ball, we found the solution. I think we can be much better in the final third."

De Zerbi bemoaned Tottenham 's decision-making with Marmoush a culprit, blazing over in the second half with Andy Robertson on an overlap and Mohammed Kudus waiting for a far-post tap in.

The former Brighton boss could see the positives but needs his men to discover their composure.

"I think we played well, in the last third we have to improve, we have to take better decisions, maybe keep calmer when we are close to doing something important.

"The chance when Marmoush shot, we had Robertson overlapping. If we take the right decision and if we play with Robertson on the second post there is Kudus to score.

"I am very happy with the spirit, with the organisation, their style of play is very clear, long ball and second ball, even the second ball we won many duels. They are good players.

"Taking a point in this stadium is not so easy. We are not happy because we didn't win but this is the right spirit and the right way to move on in this moment."

A draw was Tottenham 's eighth in the league this year, their most across a calendar year since 2020, and they failed to have a shot on target in a top-flight match for the first time since April 2022 against Brentford under Antonio Conte.

Spurs have had 38 shots in the league this season with an expected goals of 3.3 and former midfielder Danny Murphy agreed with De Zerbi over what the visitors lacked.

"When Spurs did get in really good areas, they just rushed it and shot when they maybe should've passed," he told BBC Sport.

"They made the wrong choice on pullbacks or crosses when they're getting in wide areas, taking men on one too many times when they've already got the space.

"They were just missing that little bit of calmness and composure that you expect from top quality players.

"It takes time for some players [to find chemistry]. You could argue that Marmoush and Savio know each other anyway and bright footballers quickly learn each other's runs and movements.

"From a midfielder to a forward perspective, you're not always sure what they're going to do. Whereas if you played with someone for a while, it comes more naturally. So those relationships will build."

Mykhailo Mudryk arrived on deadline day, on an initial loan from Chelsea , looking to revive his career following his four-year ban for testing positive for banned substance meldonium in 2024 , something he denied knowingly ingesting.

The Ukraine international came off the bench, his first Premier League appearance since being a second-half substitute in a 1-1 draw against Arsenal in November 2024.

"He needs time and he needs work, we have in that position Mathys Tel - big potential - but also Tel takes too many wrong decisions," added De Zerbi.

It was part of a second-half shake-up with Savio and Destiny Udogie being withdrawn after an hour in a planned double substitution on medical advice.

De Zerbi added: "Before the game the plan for Savio and Udogie was around 60 minutes. I'm not happy but football is like this, Savio not in the best physical condition to play 90 mins, he's a crucial player for us.

"Destiny is another crucial player. Kudus and Robertson played well but to start one game like today is not so easy to come inside from the bench and adapt immediately.

"I'm not happy when we have the plan but it's not my business, the management of players after injuries."
authors: Nick Mashiter at the City Ground

articles.title: Man City 1-0 Coventry: Enzo Fernandez and Iliman Ndiaye show signs of promise on debuts
articles.summary: Manchester City gave £185m of deadline-day talent their Premier League debuts in the win over Coventry - and manager Enzo Maresca will have enjoyed what he saw.
articles.body:
Manchester City gave £185m worth of talent signed on transfer deadline day their Premier League debuts in the 1-0 Premier League victory over Coventry and manager Enzo Maresca will have been quietly satisfied with what he saw from his new duo.

Midfielder Enzo Fernandez, brought in from Chelsea for £125m, was initially named as a substitute but was given a late call-up into the starting XI after Nico O'Reilly sustained a knock in the warm-up, while £60m Iliman Ndiaye also played from the off.

Both players have had limited time on the training ground with their new team-mates, but showcased early signs of what they will bring to the side and how competition for starting places has ramped up at Etihad Stadium.

Maresca knows Fernandez from his time in charge at Chelsea , with the pair winning the Europa Conference League and Club World Cup together, and he played a pivotal role in Erling Haaland's winning goal.

Maresca said: "It is much more easier when a player you already share time together [joins] because they know exactly what you want.

"We know each other very well, I know how good he is and I know that he is going to help the team to win games."

Man City maintain 100% start with win over Coventry

Players will 'learn how we want them to play'

City clung on to a nervy victory against the Sky Blues to maintain their 100% winning start to the season, but managed to get the job done courtesy of a string of saves from goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Haaland continued his fine start to the season by converting his third goal in as many games from Antoine Semenyo's deep cross, which came after Fernandez played through a slide-rule pass to the Ghanaian.

Playing in the number eight role, Argentina international Fernandez was given licence to roam and make late bursts into the box - he touched the ball six times in the opposition area, with only Haaland managing more with 11.

Fernandez could have had a dream debut but saw two shots blocked, before being replaced after 76 minutes by fellow summer signing Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international was part of City's midfield rebuild and highlights the options available to Maresca despite the departures of Bernardo Silva, Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez.

Ndiaye, meanwhile, became the first Senegalese player to represent City and is bound to give opposition defenders with his trickery and pace. No player attempted more dribbles in the match than his eight.

Maresca said: "Enzo and Iliman [played their] first game with us and then Ayyoub and Ryan [McAidoo] their first game in front of our fans.

"That is why I said there are many reasons I am happy about our win. I think they were all good.

"Ili just had two sessions with us. He needs to understand how to move. Most of the time he was moving in the wrong way, wrong position, but he needs to learn and for sure he is going to learn."

Asked to elaborate on Ndiaye's performance, Maresca said: "When Marc Guehi has the ball and he was dropping a lot and we don't need that.

"We need him in the last third so he can be a little bit more higher. That space was more for Josko Gvardiol.

"It is the same thing in this [other] side. But it is normal and with time they will learn the way we want them to play."

City's deadline-day deals make it easy to forget that England international Elliot Anderson also joined this summer for £116m from Nottingham Forest .

The 23-year-old is beginning to find his feet in a City shirt, being named man of the match against Coventry despite the travelling team threatening to cause a huge upset.

Frank Lampard's side could not take their chances and Anderson ended the game completing 143 of his 155 passes, four more than the Coventry team.

"Really impressed," said Maresca. "Not just today. He was very good against Palace; he was also very good against Bournemouth , having only been one week with us when we changed him for cramp.

"But the best thing with Elliot is the day by day. He is asking how he can learn. We sit with him one-v-one video [analysis] and he wants to be better, and that is the best thing for any player."

Former England international Lampard added: "He is a really good player. I admire him from afar and did at Forest, but this was the first time I had seen him close up in the flesh.

"Very smart, very talented and a very good player - good brain, everything you need in a midfield player - and he is going to be a fantastic player for Manchester City .

"He had a lot of the ball today. I don't think he could hurt us, but he was constantly on it and I highly respect players like that, no doubt."

articles.title: El Inter se saca una remontada de campeón antes de visitar el Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: Levantaron un 0-2 en contra con doblete de Lautaro y otro gol de Thuram
articles.summary: Levantaron un 0-2 en contra con doblete de Lautaro y otro gol de Thuram
articles.body: A tres días de visitar el Santiago Bernabéu, el Inter demostró en el Meazza por qué es el campeón de la Serie A. Los de Chivu remontaron un 0-2 en contra ante el Nápoles y acabaron ganando 3-2 con un tanto de Lautaro Martínez en el descuento. El argentino firmó doblete y Marcus Thuram, que está de vuelta, el otro restante. En la previa de su viaje a Madrid, Chivu apostaba por la Serie A y únicamente reservaba a Calhanoglu. Thuram, que no ha sido titular en este arranque de curso, volvía a ser suplente. Y Diouf, relevo de Dumfries por ahora en el costado derecho, fue el primer protagonista forzando a Meret a realizar una gran parada a los dos minutos de iniciar el duelo en el Meazza. Fue un partido de ritmo alto, sin dominador claro, con ambos equipos teniendo diferentes tramos de dominio. Si el Inter aceleraba, generaba mucho... pero no había prisa en los vigentes campeones del 'Scudetto'. De hecho, fue Zambo Anguissa el que tomó el relevo de Diouf y, en la portería contrario, forzó dos muy buenas manos del español Josep Martínez. Pero el Inter acabó 'mandando' y cerró el primer tiempo con un disparo de falta al palo de Dimarco y una ocasión de Lautaro. La segunda parte fue directamente una locura. Curtis Jones y Thuram entraron al descanso pero el Nápoles respondía con un gol de Politano a los dos minutos de la reanudación. Y tras un paradón de Meret en la réplica interista, otro gol del Napoli: Hojlund. El Inter sacó entonces la artillería y el orgullo, y aprovechó también una defensa napolitana que (a falta de Badiashile, Buongiorno y Beukema) sigue haciendo aguas. Lautaro hizo el primero tras una gran asociación entre Zielinski y Dimarco, Thuram el segundo... y cuando todo apuntaba al empate, de nuevo 'Lauti' apareció en la selva del área pequeña para desatar la locura en Lombardía. Para el Inter es un pleno de triunfos: victorias sobre Monza, Cagliari... y ahora, el Nápoles. Peor le va a los de Allegri con dos derrotas consecutivas ante Como e Inter.

articles.title: Barcelona make Lautaro Martinez move as Inter chief Giuseppe Marotta reveals details of Barca’s inquiry
articles.summary: Barcelona made an enquiry about Lautaro Martinez during the summer, but Inter Milan were clear about their stance on their captain. Inter president Giuseppe...
articles.body:
Barcelona made an enquiry about Lautaro Martinez during the summer, but Inter Milan were clear about their stance on their captain.

Inter president Giuseppe Marotta has now confirmed that the Catalan club did make contact over the Argentine striker, although the response from both the Italian side and the player was decisive.

Barcelona set sights on Lautaro Martinez

Speaking to DAZN Italia ahead of Inter's meeting with Napoli at San Siro, Marotta addressed Barcelona's interest in Martinez and made it clear that the forward remains central to the club's plans.

"The news about Barcelona's enquiry regarding Lautaro is true, but the response was decisive from us and from the player to continue together."

Martinez's position at Inter appears to have played a major role in the club's determination to keep hold of him. Marotta highlighted the importance of the Argentine to the team, pointing to both his leadership and his long-term value to the club.

"Lautaro is the team's captain and embodies Inter's present and future, and we hope this harmony will continue for the long term."

While Barcelona's interest was genuine, Marotta's comments indicate that Inter were not prepared to let the enquiry develop into a transfer.

The club's position was matched by Martinez himself, with the striker choosing to continue his relationship with the Italian champions rather than pursue a move away.

For Inter, retaining their captain means keeping a player Marotta considers important not only to the team's current ambitions but also to their future.

The president's comments therefore provide a clear answer to the speculation surrounding Barcelona's interest. The enquiry happened, but neither Inter nor Martinez wanted to take the next step.

Instead, the Argentine remains with Inter, with Marotta hoping the understanding between the player and the club can continue for years to come.

articles.title: Oregon Football vs. Boise State Game Thread
articles.summary: The Ducks will open the 2026 season with a challenging BSU Broncos team
articles.body:
Eugene experienced a very unusual, heavy late-summer storm of the type we don't generally see until October or so, and we had two days of thunderstorms and heavy rain on Thursday and Friday.

BSU's flight to Eugene was not spared from the storm's wrath, and the team had to divert to Portland and take the two-hour bus ride to get to Eugene late yesterday.

Boise St. has historically given then Ducks problems, most recently in 2024 when the No. 7 Ducks got past the Broncos on a late field goal to win, 37-34.

That probably won't replay today, but you never know. The books, however, aren't giving BSU much love – The Broncos are 24.5 point underdogs today.

Right now, it's sunny and 62° in Eugene (at 11:00 am local time) and should be 66 and climbing by kickoff.

articles.title: Ten Hag closes the door on Barcelona move for Ruud Nijstad: ‘He wants to stay here’
articles.summary: FC Barcelona closely monitored Ruud Nijstad during the summer transfer window, with the 18-year-old regarded as one of the most promising young defenders in...
articles.body:
FC Barcelona closely monitored Ruud Nijstad during the summer transfer window, with the 18-year-old regarded as one of the most promising young defenders in Dutch football.

However, FC Twente refused to consider his departure, even rejecting an €8 million offer from the La Liga champions .

Despite being thwarted, the Blaugrana have continued to monitor Nijstad, with an eye on a potential move in the January transfer window .

However, Twente's technical director, Erik ten Hag, has revealed that Nijstad never indicated that he wanted to leave the club, despite attracting interest from several major sides.

"There's a great deal of interest in Ruud from some very big clubs. That's no secret," Ten Hag told RTV Oost, as quoted by SPORT .

Barcelona are interested in Nijstad. (Photo courtesy: X/fctwente)

The former Manchester United manager was nevertheless clear that Nijstad never tried to force through a transfer.

"He wants to stay here. We didn't renew his contract by chance. He wants to continue his development here, at least this season, succeed with us, and then we'll see what happens," Ten Hag explained.

Nijstad extended his Twente contract in June, committing his future to the Dutch club until 2029. The new agreement was intended to protect one of the brightest prospects to emerge from the club's academy.

Barcelona's interest became particularly strong during the summer. As mentioned previously, the Catalan club submitted an offer of around €8 million for the centre-back, but Twente rejected it because they were looking for a higher fee.

Nijstad's contract runs until 2029. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images for DFB)

Ten Hag remained firm throughout the negotiations, making it clear that Twente had no intention of letting the teenager leave.

Twente's plan is now for Nijstad to continue his development with the first team this season before reassessing his situation in the future.

Barcelona will therefore have to wait if they want to revive their interest in one of the Netherlands' most highly rated young centre-backs.

January could provide another opportunity for the Blaugrana , although Twente's current stance suggests the club will continue to make keeping Nijstad a priority.
